question.:question/problem:
Find an antiderivative. Include the constant $C$.

$$
\int - 9 x^{2} \cot{\left(x^{3} \right)} \csc{\left(x^{3} \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x
$$

{{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $u=x^{3}$. Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=3 x^{2}.
$$

Substituting, including the required constant factor, gives

$$
\int - 9 x^{2} \cot{\left(x^{3} \right)} \csc{\left(x^{3} \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x=-3\left(\int \cot{\left(u \right)} \csc{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).
$$

Integrate with respect to $u$:

$$
-3\left(\int \cot{\left(u \right)} \csc{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right)=3 \csc{\left(u \right)}+C.
$$

Substitute back:

$$
3 \csc{\left(x^{3} \right)}+C.
$$

$$

Let $u=3 x^{3} - \frac{\pi}{4}$. Then

$$
\frac{\mathrm{d}u}{\mathrm{d}x}=9 x^{2}.
$$

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\frac{\sqrt[3]{30} \sqrt[3]{\pi}}{6}&\Longrightarrow u=\frac{\pi}{6}\\x=\frac{6^{\frac{2}{3}} \sqrt[3]{\pi}}{6}&\Longrightarrow u=\frac{\pi}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting, including the required constant factor, gives

$$
\int_{\frac{\sqrt[3]{30} \sqrt[3]{\pi}}{6}}^{\frac{6^{\frac{2}{3}} \sqrt[3]{\pi}}{6}} - x^{2} \cos{\left(3 x^{3} - \frac{\pi}{4} \right)}\,\mathrm{d}x=- \frac{1}{9}\left(\int_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}} \cos{\left(u \right)}\,\mathrm{d}u\right).
$$

Integrate and evaluate at both bounds:

$$
\left[- \frac{\sin{\left(u \right)}}{9}\right]_{\frac{\pi}{6}}^{\frac{\pi}{4}}=\left(- \frac{\sqrt{2}}{18}\right)-\left(- \frac{1}{18}\right).
$$

Simplifying gives

$$
\frac{1}{18} - \frac{\sqrt{2}}{18}.
$$
